links.comparator_used: No head-to-head comparator; the study simulated the LLM-report-classification framework against CVPED outputs, with human review of discrepancies, and did not compare it with manual chart review
links.outcome: Drift detection and incremental PE case detection when CVPED outputs were compared with LLM classification of radiology reports
links.effect: 373/11,999 (3.1%) discrepant classifications; 29 alerts among 111 CVPED-positive/LLM-negative cases, of which 24 were CVPED false-positives, 1 an LLM false-negative, and 4 true alerts for incremental PE; a 2.5% drop in LLM specificity gave a 1.7-fold increase in discrepancies, detected in 22 days; optimal retrospective assessment period 2 months
links.tradeoff: Most alerts were false alarms (24 of 29 were CVPED false-positives), so human review of discrepancies was required; detection of a specificity drop took about 22 days; a 10% drop in sensitivity was needed to produce a discrepancy rise similar to a 2-3% specificity drop
links.quote: Of those, 24 were CVPED false-positives, 1 was an LLM false-negative, and the framework ultimately identified 4 true-alerts for incremental PE cases.

design_hint: postdeployment monitoring and drift detection with LLM oversight
